Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of the digit 7 in the number $5.074$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths. In $5.074$ the digit 0 is in the tenths place, 7 is in the hundredths place and 4 in the thousandths place. So the digit 7 stands for $\frac{7}{100}=0.07$. The trap is to give $70$ or $7$, which ignore the position after the decimal point. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of $x^5,\ x^3,\ x^9$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The HCF of powers of the same letter is that letter raised to the smallest exponent. The exponents are 5, 3 and 9; the smallest is 3, so the HCF is $x^3$. Option D is the L.C.M, not the HCF. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Arranging the decimals $0.33,\ 0.42,\ 0.25$ in ascending order gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Ascending means from the smallest to the largest. Compare the tenths first: $0.25<0.33<0.42$. Option B is the descending order; C and D are not ordered. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The number line that represents the set of elements in the set $T=\{x:0\leq x\leq 5\}$ is

![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In $0\leq x\leq 5$ both ends are included (the sign is $\leq$ on both sides), so both ends are drawn with filled circles. Line A has two open circles, line B an open circle on the right only, and line D an open circle on the left only. Only line C has two filled circles. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The number $-5$ belongs to the set

*Options as printed:* A) Natural numbers   B) Rational numbers   C) Irrational numbers   D) Integers
questions.corrige_markdown:
The number $-5$ is a negative whole number, so it is an integer. It is not a natural number (natural numbers are never negative) and it is not irrational (it can be written as the fraction $\frac{-5}{1}$). However, every integer is also a rational number, so the option "Rational numbers" is true as well: two of the four options are correct.

**Intended answer: D (Integers), the most specific set.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The fraction "two and one fifth" in figures gives
questions.corrige_markdown: "Two and one fifth" is the mixed number made of the whole number 2 and the fraction $\frac{1}{5}$, written $2\frac{1}{5}$ (which equals $\frac{11}{5}$). Option C swaps the whole part and the numerator; B has no whole part. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number $234.5\times10^{3}$ written in standard form is
questions.corrige_markdown: Write $234.5=2.345\times10^{2}$. Then $234.5\times10^{3}=2.345\times10^{2}\times10^{3}=2.345\times10^{2+3}=2.345\times10^{5}$. The trap is to forget to add the $10^2$ coming from the shift of the decimal point. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number $17.561$ correct to the nearest whole number is
questions.corrige_markdown: To round to the nearest whole number look at the first decimal digit: it is 5, so we round up. $17.561\approx 18$. Options B and D are rounded to one decimal place, and C would be correct only if the first decimal digit were 4 or less. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a class of 105 students, there are 60 girls. The ratio of boys to girls is
questions.corrige_markdown: Number of boys $=105-60=45$. Ratio boys : girls $=45:60$. Divide both numbers by 15: $3:4$. Option A is the ratio girls : boys, and B and D use the total (105 = 7 x 15). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The rate at which $2{,}000{,}000$ FCFA is invested for 2 years to yield an interest of $200{,}000$ FCFA is
questions.corrige_markdown: Use simple interest $I=\frac{P\times R\times T}{100}$. Then $200000=\frac{2000000\times R\times 2}{100}$, so $200000=40000R$ and $R=\frac{200000}{40000}=5$. The rate is $5\%$ per annum. The trap is to forget the 2 years ($10\%$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An empty set is represented as
questions.corrige_markdown: An empty set has no element at all, and it is written $\{\ \}$ or $\varnothing$. Option A, $\{\varnothing\}$, is a set with one element (the empty set), and C, $\{0\}$, is a set with one element (the number 0). Option D is the letter O, not a set. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the set $M=\{\text{prime factors of } 25\}$, $M$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $25=5\times5$, so its only prime factor is 5. Therefore $M=\{5\}$. Option A lists all the factors of 25 (but 1 and 25 are not prime), B contains 25 which is not prime, and D contains 10 which is not even a factor of 25. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In set notation, the number of elements in $P$ and not in $Q$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: "In $P$ and not in $Q$" means in $P$ AND in the complement of $Q$, which is $P\cap Q'$. The number of its elements is $n(P\cap Q')$. $P'\cap Q$ is the opposite (in $Q$ but not in $P$), $P\cap Q$ is the overlap, and $Q'\cup P$ would include everything outside $Q$ as well. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that

$p$: John is a Cameroonian

$q$: John is bilingual,

the statement "If John is bilingual then he is a Cameroonian" can be represented as
questions.corrige_markdown: The statement has the form "If (condition) then (conclusion)". The condition is "John is bilingual", that is $q$, and the conclusion is "he is a Cameroonian", that is $p$. So the statement is $q\to p$. The trap is to reverse the two parts and write $p\to q$. (Option A is printed $p\to p$ in the paper, a probable misprint of $p\to q$; it is wrong either way.) **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mapping for which $x$ maps to $2x+1$ is called
questions.corrige_markdown: For $x\mapsto 2x+1$, each input gives exactly one output, and two different inputs never give the same output (if $2a+1=2b+1$ then $a=b$). So the mapping is one-one. A many-one mapping would need two inputs with the same output, as in $x\mapsto x^2$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x)=3-2x$, then $f(-1)$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Replace $x$ by $-1$: $f(-1)=3-2(-1)=3+2=5$. The trap is the sign: $-2\times(-1)=+2$, not $-2$ (which would give 1). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the function $f:x\mapsto3x+1$ and $g:x\mapsto2x$, $fg(x)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $fg(x)$ means $f(g(x))$: apply $g$ first, then $f$. $g(x)=2x$, so $fg(x)=f(2x)=3(2x)+1=6x+1$. Option C, $6x+2$, is $gf(x)=2(3x+1)$, obtained by applying the functions in the wrong order. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The point at which two lines meet is called an

*Options as printed:* A) angle   B) intercept   C) edge   D) origin
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two lines that meet (cross) do so at a single point, which is called their **point of intersection**. None of the four printed options is this term: an angle is the opening between two lines, an intercept is a point where a line cuts an axis, an edge is where two faces of a solid meet, and the origin is the point $(0,0)$ where the two axes meet. The nearest word is "intercept" (probably a misprint of "intersection"), but the printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

**Intended answer: point of intersection (not among the printed options).**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the interior angle of a polygon is $76^\circ$, its exterior angle is
questions.corrige_markdown: Interior and exterior angles at the same vertex lie on a straight line, so they add up to $180^\circ$: exterior angle $=180^\circ-76^\circ=104^\circ$. Option B is $90^\circ-76^\circ$, a wrong complement. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A regular solid with 11 nets is a
questions.corrige_markdown: A cube has exactly 11 different nets (arrangements of six squares that fold into a cube). A square is a plane shape, not a solid, a cylinder has a curved surface, and a cuboid is not a regular solid. So the answer is the cube. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a construction, $PQ$ is a perpendicular bisector of $RS$ at $T$. The value of the angle $PTS$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: A perpendicular bisector cuts the segment $RS$ at its midpoint $T$ and makes a right angle with it. Hence $\angle PTS=90^\circ$. The trap is to confuse it with an angle bisector (which would give $45^\circ$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given that $l_1$ and $l_2$ are parallel lines in figure 1, and $l_3$ is a transversal with angle $b=85^\circ$, the value of angle $a$ is

![fig-2](gce-ol-maths-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Angle $b$ lies above $l_1$ on the right of the transversal. Its corresponding angle on $l_2$ (above $l_2$, right of $l_3$) is also $85^\circ$ because $l_1\parallel l_2$. Angle $a$ lies above $l_2$ on the LEFT of $l_3$, so it forms a straight line with that angle: $a=180^\circ-85^\circ=95^\circ$. The trap is to take $a=b=85^\circ$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The circumference of a circle in terms of $\pi$, with radius 3 cm is
questions.corrige_markdown: $C=2\pi r=2\times\pi\times3=6\pi$ cm. Option D, $9\pi$, comes from the area formula $\pi r^2$ (in cm$^2$), and A forgets the factor 2. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The area of a rectangle with dimensions 9 cm by 3 cm is
questions.corrige_markdown: Area $=$ length $\times$ width $=9\times3=27\text{ cm}^2$. Option A is the sum $9+3$, B is the perimeter $2(9+3)$, and C is $2\times27$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The volume of a cone with base radius 3 cm and height 7 cm, taking $\pi$ as $\frac{22}{7}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $V=\frac{1}{3}\pi r^2h=\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{22}{7}\times3^2\times7=\frac{1}{3}\times22\times9=66\text{ cm}^3$. Option B, $198\text{ cm}^3$, is the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height (the factor $\frac13$ was forgotten). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The $y$-intercept of the line $3y+4x=12$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The $y$-intercept is the value of $y$ where the line cuts the $y$-axis, that is where $x=0$. Then $3y=12$, so $y=4$. Option B, 3, is the $x$-intercept ($y=0$ gives $x=3$). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The lines with equations $y=m_1x+c$ and $y=m_2x+k$ are perpendicular if
questions.corrige_markdown: Two lines are perpendicular when the product of their gradients is $-1$: $m_1m_2=-1$. Option C ($m_1=m_2$) is the condition for parallel lines. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The graph of the function $f(x)=2x^2-3x-2$ has
questions.corrige_markdown: $f$ is a quadratic function and the coefficient of $x^2$ is $2>0$, so the parabola opens upwards. It has exactly one turning point, the lowest point of the curve, which is a minimum (at $x=\frac{3}{4}$, where $f=-\frac{25}{8}$). A maximum point would need a negative coefficient of $x^2$. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: both maximum and minimum turning points

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of factors in the expression $(x+1)(x+2)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The expression is a product of two brackets, $(x+1)$ and $(x+2)$, which are its two factors. So the number of factors is 2. The trap is to expand the brackets to $x^2+3x+2$ (three terms) and count terms instead of factors. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Simplifying $8a+3+5-3a$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Collect like terms: $8a-3a=5a$ and $3+5=8$. So $8a+3+5-3a=5a+8$. Option B adds $8a$ and $3a$ instead of subtracting. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Simplifying $2^2\times2^{-3}$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the exponents: $2^2\times2^{-3}=2^{2+(-3)}=2^{-1}$ (which equals $\frac12$). Option B adds the absolute values, and D multiplies the exponents. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the formula $A=\pi r^2$, expressing $r$ in terms of $A$ and $\pi$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Divide both sides by $\pi$: $r^2=\frac{A}{\pi}$. Then take the square root: $r=\sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}$. Option A forgets the square root, and C takes the square root of $A$ only. Option D equals $\frac{A}{\pi}$ since $\sqrt{\pi^2}=\pi$, so it is the same as A. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The next term in the sequence $1,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3,\ 5,\ \ldots$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Each term is the sum of the two terms before it: $1+1=2$, $1+2=3$, $2+3=5$. So the next term is $3+5=8$ (this is the Fibonacci sequence). Options A, B and C do not follow this rule. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $y$ varies directly as $x$, the equation connecting $y$ and $x$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: "$y$ varies directly as $x$" means $y\propto x$, and removing the proportionality sign with a constant of variation $k$ gives the equation $y=kx$. Options A and D describe inverse variation. Option B is the proportionality statement itself, not an equation, and the question asks for the equation. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The solution set of the inequality $3x-4\leq8$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Add 4 to both sides: $3x\leq12$. Divide by 3 (a positive number, so the sign does not change): $x\leq4$. The solution set is $\{x:x\leq4\}$. Options C and D come from forgetting to add 4 before dividing ($\frac{4}{3}$ is the value of $x$ in $3x=4$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a network with 4 vertices and 5 edges, the number of regions is
questions.corrige_markdown: For a connected planar network Euler's formula is $V-E+R=2$, where $R$ counts all the regions including the outside one. Then $R=2-V+E=2-4+5=3$. Option B counts only the inside regions (2) and forgets the outside one, and 5 is just the number of edges. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the right-angled triangle $PQR$ in figure 2, the adjacent side to the angle $\theta$ is

![fig-3](gce-ol-maths-2025-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The right angle is at $Q$ and $\theta$ is the angle at $P$. The hypotenuse (opposite the right angle) is $PR$. The side opposite $\theta$ is $QR$. The side adjacent to $\theta$ (next to it, and not the hypotenuse) is $PQ$. Option D, $PQR$, names the triangle, not a side. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of $\frac{\sin30^\circ}{\cos30^\circ}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $\frac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\tan\theta$, so the value is $\tan30^\circ$. With $\sin30^\circ=\frac12$ and $\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$: $\frac{1/2}{\sqrt3/2}=\frac{1}{\sqrt3}\ (\approx0.577)$. Option A is $\tan60^\circ$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the angle of elevation of a man lying on the ground and sees a bird on top of a tree at $P$ is $40^\circ$, the angle of depression of the bird is
questions.corrige_markdown: The line of sight from the man to the bird makes $40^\circ$ with the horizontal ground (angle of elevation). The line of sight from the bird back to the man makes an angle of depression with the horizontal at the bird. These two angles are alternate angles between parallel horizontal lines, so they are equal: $40^\circ$. The trap is to give $50^\circ=90^\circ-40^\circ$, which is the angle with the vertical. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\begin{pmatrix}7\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{b}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-9\end{pmatrix}$, then $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Add the components one by one: $\begin{pmatrix}7+2\\3+(-9)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}9\\-6\end{pmatrix}$. Option A is $\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}$ ($2-7$ and $-9-3$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The vector $\mathbf{OP}=\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}$ lies in the
questions.corrige_markdown: $\mathbf{OP}=\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\-1\end{pmatrix}$, so $P$ is the point $(1,-1)$: positive $x$ and negative $y$. That is the 4th quadrant (bottom right), the quadrants being numbered anticlockwise from the top right. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The magnitude of the vector $-5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $|-5\mathbf{i}+12\mathbf{j}|=\sqrt{(-5)^2+12^2}=\sqrt{25+144}=\sqrt{169}=13$. Option A is $\sqrt{144-25}$ (subtracting instead of adding), and C is $12-5$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\2\end{pmatrix}$, $A^{T}=$
questions.corrige_markdown: The transpose turns the columns into rows without changing the order of the entries. The column $\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\2\end{pmatrix}$ becomes the row $\begin{pmatrix}3&4&2\end{pmatrix}$. Option B is $A$ itself, and C and D reorder the entries. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of $m$ for which $\begin{pmatrix}m+2&3\\4&-3\end{pmatrix}$ is a singular matrix is
questions.corrige_markdown: A matrix is singular when its determinant is 0. $\det=(m+2)(-3)-3\times4=-3m-6-12=-3m-18$. Setting $-3m-18=0$ gives $m=-6$. Check: with $m=-6$ the matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}-4&3\\4&-3\end{pmatrix}$ and $(-4)(-3)-3\times4=12-12=0$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The coordinates of the point $A(1,3)$ reflected in the $x$-axis are
questions.corrige_markdown: A reflection in the $x$-axis keeps the $x$-coordinate and changes the sign of the $y$-coordinate: $(x,y)\to(x,-y)$. So $A(1,3)\to(1,-3)$. Option B is the reflection in the $y$-axis, and C is the reflection in the origin. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the matrices $P=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\4&5\end{pmatrix}$ and $Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&-7\end{pmatrix}$, $P+Q$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Add the entries in the same positions: $\begin{pmatrix}2+1&3+2\\4+3&5+(-7)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}3&5\\7&-2\end{pmatrix}$. Option D has the sign of the last entry wrong ($5-7=-2$, not $+2$); A and C are $P-Q$ and $Q-P$ with the wrong signs. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The mode, median and mean are collectively called the measures of
questions.corrige_markdown: Mode, median and mean each describe the centre (a typical value) of a data set, so they are called measures of central tendency. Measures of dispersion (range, standard deviation) describe how spread out the data are. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The median of the marks $3,\ 7,\ 9,\ 11$ and $13$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The marks are already in order and there are 5 of them, so the median is the middle (3rd) one: $9$. The value $8.6$ is the mean: $\frac{3+7+9+11+13}{5}=\frac{43}{5}=8.6$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The range of the scores $3,\ 2,\ 0,\ 5,\ 6,\ 4$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Range $=$ largest score $-$ smallest score $=6-0=6$. The mean of the scores is $\frac{20}{6}\approx3.3$, which is not asked here. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The probability that John does his Mathematics assignment is $0.6$. Then the probability that he does not do it is
questions.corrige_markdown: Doing and not doing the assignment are complementary events, so $P(\text{not do})=1-0.6=0.4$. **Answer: C.**
